Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield of Colorado  
Appeals Department  
[Appeals mailing address or submission method provided by Anthem]

Re: Expedited or standard pre-service appeal of denial  
Member: Riley Ellison  
Member ID: W168862914  
Reference number: POC-ACAA2D5BAD-67552  
Requested service: C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion  
CPT: 22551  
Treating surgeon: Lindqvist, MD

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Anthem’s denial of the requested C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion. The denial states only that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. I request that Anthem reverse the denial and authorize the procedure.

The clinical record establishes a confirmed structural diagnosis and a corresponding neurologic deficit. Riley has experienced nine months of progressive neck pain that has not been relieved by rest. The June 7, 2026 cervical MRI shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root. Riley has radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, together with weakness. Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on MRI.

The requested operation is directed at the documented pathology. CPT 22551 is being requested for a single-level C5-C6 anterior cervical decompression and fusion to relieve the documented C6 nerve-root compression and stabilize the treated level.

Conservative treatment has been substantial and unsuccessful:

- Supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, was completed for eight weeks from May 13, 2026, through July 8, 2026, for 24 visits. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment.
- NSAIDs were used for eight months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 18, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, the patient continues to have progressive pain, radicular symptoms, numbness, and weakness.

The record also supports the safety and appropriateness of proceeding. There is no active infection or untreated substance use. Riley is a nonsmoker, has a BMI of 29, and has been evaluated by Lindqvist, MD, an orthopedic surgeon.

The publicly available Carelon Spine Surgery guideline retrieved for this appeal describes the relevant cervical surgery as treatment commonly used for cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy, with the goal of decompressing the nerve roots or spinal cord and stabilizing the spine. The same guideline states that medical-necessity review should consider confirmation of the diagnosis through clinical evaluation and diagnostic testing, whether the expected benefit outweighs potential harms, whether accepted medical practice supports the intervention, and whether the intervention is reasonably likely to improve the patient’s outcome. The records summarized above address each of those considerations: the diagnosis is confirmed by MRI and examination, the symptoms correspond anatomically to the compressed C6 nerve root, extensive conservative treatment has failed, and the proposed operation directly treats the compression.

I am not quoting Anthem’s member-specific denial criteria because the denial notice did not identify or provide the exact plan criteria, version, or clinical-review rationale applied to this request. Please provide the complete criteria and clinical-review basis used for this determination, including the specific deficiencies Anthem believes remain. Please also consider the enclosed MRI report, physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection history, examination findings, and surgeon’s clinical documentation.

Based on the documented neurologic compression, corresponding symptoms and weakness, progressive course, failure of conservative treatment, and absence of the listed safety concerns, the requested C5-C6 ACDF meets medical-necessity requirements. Please overturn the denial and issue authorization for CPT 22551.

If Anthem continues to deny the request, please provide a detailed written explanation identifying each criterion that was not met, the clinical evidence relied upon, the reviewer’s qualifications, and the instructions for any further internal or external review.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received by January 29, 2027.

Sincerely,

Riley Ellison  
[Mailing address]

[Email address]
